issues.legal_issue: A new contention about the legal effect of a grant may be considered on appeal when it turns solely on construing the document and does not depend on disputed facts.
material_facts: The defendants raised the contention that the grant incorporated the lands into an existing Patni only in appeal, not in the trial court.
The contention depended on construing the grant, and there was no dispute about how its terms related to existing facts.
No objection was made when the contention was raised in the first appeal.
issues.conclusion: The appellate court was right to allow the contention to be raised.
issues.legal_principle: The construction of a contract or grant must be based on the document's terms; evidence is inadmissible on that question where there is no dispute about how the document relates to existing facts. The Court relied on Balkishen Das v. Legge (1899) and Maung Kyin v. Ma Shwe La (1917).

rule.if: appellate_proceeding and new_document_construction_ground and document_terms_undisputed and no_factual_evidence_needed

predicates.appellate_proceeding: The matter is being considered in an appeal.
predicates.new_document_construction_ground: A party raises a contention on appeal about the legal effect of a document that was not raised at trial.
predicates.document_terms_undisputed: The parties do not dispute the document's terms or how those terms relate to existing facts.
predicates.no_factual_evidence_needed: Deciding the contention requires no factual inquiry or evidence beyond construing the document.

issues.definition: When an appellate proceeding involves a newly raised document-construction ground, and the document's terms are undisputed and no factual evidence is needed, the ground may be considered.

issues.legal_issue: A grant of resumed service lands to an existing tenure-holder creates a distinct tenure when its terms show that the parties intended the lands to be independently held and separately saleable for rent arrears.
material_facts: The service lands had been resumed, assessed, and transferred to the estate-holder subject to pre-existing contracts and rights.
The estate-holder granted the lands to the holders of the village's existing Patni interest under a document fixing rent for the lands.
The grant provided that the lands themselves could be sold under the applicable sale procedure if rent was unpaid, and provided separately for their transfer and succession.
The grant also linked the lands' tenure to the existing village tenure in specified circumstances and preserved the rights of any other persons holding interests in that tenure.
The estate-holder later sold the granted lands after a sale for rent arrears, and the purchaser sued to recover possession.
issues.conclusion: The grant created a distinct Patni, and the sale of the lands for arrears was valid; the purchaser acquired good title.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 48, 50 and 51 of the Village Chaukidari Act, 1870, resumed Chaukidari Chakaran lands were transferred subject to prior contracts; absent a different agreement, a Patnidar's rights ordinarily continued on the same basis as the original Patni. The parties could, however, agree to create a distinct Patni, permanent, heritable and alienable, independently subject to rent and sale for default. The Court relied on Ranjit Singh v. Maharaj Bahadur Singh, Bhupendra Narayan Singh v. Narapat Singh, Rajendra Nath Mukherjee v. Hiralal Mukherjee, and Gopendra Chandra v. Taraprasanna on rights in resumed lands; on Mohadeb Mundul v. Cowell and Monomothonath Dev v. Glascott concerning separate tenures and sale; and on Forbes v. Git for construing conflicting clauses. The document must be read as a whole, preferring a construction that gives effect to its terms; an earlier clause prevails over a later clause that destroys its effect. The Court distinguished Kanchan Barani Debi v. Umesh Chandra.

rule.if: tenure_sale_dispute and resumed_service_lands_granted_to_existing_tenure_holders and grant_fixes_separate_rent and grant_allows_separate_sale_for_rent_default and grant_provides_for_separate_transfer_or_succession

predicates.tenure_sale_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether a sale of granted lands for unpaid rent was valid and whether the purchaser obtained title to those lands.
predicates.resumed_service_lands_granted_to_existin: Lands formerly held for village service were resumed and then granted to persons who already held a tenure in the village.
predicates.grant_fixes_separate_rent: The grant sets rent specifically for the granted lands.
predicates.grant_allows_separate_sale_for_rent_defa: The grant provides that the granted lands may themselves be sold if their rent is unpaid.
predicates.grant_provides_for_separate_transfer_or_: The grant makes provision for transfer of, or succession to, the granted lands as a tenure held separately from the village tenure.

issues.definition: Where a sale dispute concerns resumed service lands granted to existing tenure-holders, and the grant fixes rent for those lands, permits their separate sale for rent default, and provides for their separate transfer or succession, the grant creates a distinct tenure and a separate sale is valid.
